title: AA Batteries 8-pack

drivers.name: 10% off promotion
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted uplift x1.17 from 7 past promotions; this week's 5.1% price cut is deeper than most past 10% off events, and it's the first in 18 months. Stronger than average lift expected.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery warning
drivers.evidence: Planner note indicates supply risk. This could reduce available stock and dampen demand. Adjust down to reflect potential stockouts.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 34.8. Thanksgiving has a historical median lift of x1.4, but the noise-adjusted estimate is x1.0—insufficient evidence to justify a lift. The 10% off promotion has a noise-adjusted uplift of x1.17 from 7 past events, consistent with the classical model. However, the price drop is deeper (5.1%) than any prior promotion (max 30% off but only once), and this is the first 10% off in 18 months. The supplier warning adds downside risk. Given thin evidence and the price change being deeper than past promotions, shrink the uplift toward 1.0. The final adjustment is a moderate 10% lift, with slightly widened downside due to supply risk.

  shelf price: 9.73 (-5.1% vs regular price 10.25)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 34.8 | 5%-95%: 17.9 - 58.9 | 10%-90%: 20.3 - 55.7

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-44% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
